entries.sanskrit:
एकोनत्रिंशके भक्ति-योगस् तु बहुधोच्यते ।

कालस्य च बलं घोरा संसृतिश् च विरक्तये ॥

उक्तानुवाद-पूर्वकं भक्ति-मार्ग-भेदान् पृच्छति द्वाभ्याम् । लक्षणं महद्-आदीनां यथा साङ्ख्येषु तथा कथितम् । येन लक्षणेन तत् पारमार्थिकं परस्पर-विभक्तम् इत्य् अर्थः । यो भक्ति-योगो मूलं प्रयोजनं यस्य तद् यन्-मूलम्, तत् कथितम् । तस्य भक्ति-योगस्य मार्गं प्रकारं विस्तरशो मे ब्रूहि ॥१-२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
ekonatriṃśake bhakti-yogas tu bahudhocyate |

kālasya ca balaṃ ghorā saṃsṛtiś ca viraktaye ||

uktānuvāda-pūrvakaṃ bhakti-mārga-bhedān pṛcchati dvābhyām | lakṣaṇaṃ mahad-ādīnāṃ yathā sāṅkhyeṣu tathā kathitam | yena lakṣaṇena tat pāramārthikaṃ paraspara-vibhaktam ity arthaḥ | yo bhakti-yogo mūlaṃ prayojanaṃ yasya tad yan-mūlam, tat kathitam | tasya bhakti-yogasya mārgaṃ prakāraṃ vistaraśo me brūhi ||1-2||
entries.literal_english: In the twenty-ninth chapter the many forms of bhakti-yoga are explained, together with the power of Time and the dreadful course of transmigration, in order to produce detachment. Restating what has already been taught, Devahūti asks in two verses for the distinctions among the paths of devotion. Just as the characteristics of mahat and the other principles were explained in Sāṅkhya so that each could be truly distinguished from the others, she asks Kapila to explain at length the modes of that bhakti-yoga which is the root and purpose of the teaching.

entries.sanskrit: येन संसृतीनाम् आख्यानेन विगत-रागो भवेत् ॥३॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: yena saṃsṛtīnām ākhyānena vigata-rāgo bhavet ||3||
entries.literal_english: By hearing the account of the courses of transmigration, one may become free from attachment.

entries.sanskrit: ईश्वर-रूपस्य महा-प्रभावस्य ते त्वद्-आत्मकस्य । यद् धेतोर् यद् भयात् कुशलं पूण्यं कुर्वन्ति ॥४॥
word_for_word: of the form of the Lord
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: īśvara-rūpasya mahā-prabhāvasya te tvad-ātmakasya | yad dhetor yad bhayāt kuśalaṃ pūṇyaṃ kurvanti ||4||
entries.literal_english: Time is the form of the Lord, of immense power and identical with Him. From fear of that Time people perform wholesome and meritorious acts.

entries.sanskrit: अचक्षुषोऽज्ञस्य । अतो मिथ्या-भूते देहादाव् अभिमतिर् अहङ्कारो यस्य । अतः कर्मसु अनुविद्धया आसक्तया धिया श्रान्तस्य । अत एवानाश्रयेऽपारे तमसि संसारे चिरं प्रसुप्तस्य लोकस्य प्रबोधाय त्वं योग-प्रकाशको भास्करः किलाविर्भूतोऽसि ॥५॥
word_for_word: identification with body etc. is ego
by an intellect bound to actions
in the shoreless darkness of saṃsāra
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: acakṣuṣo’jñasya | ato mithyā-bhūte dehādāv abhimatir ahaṅkāro yasya | ataḥ karmasu anuviddhayā āsaktayā dhiyā śrāntasya | ata evānāśraye’pāre tamasi saṃsāre ciraṃ prasuptasya lokasya prabodhāya tvaṃ yoga-prakāśako bhāskaraḥ kilāvirbhūto’si ||5||
entries.literal_english: For the sightless—that is, the ignorant—ego consists in identification with the unreal body and the rest. Exhausted by an intellect bound to actions and long asleep in the unsupported, shoreless darkness of saṃsāra, the world is to be awakened; for that purpose You have appeared as the sun that reveals yoga.

entries.sanskrit: श्लक्ष्णं सुन्दरम् ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: “Ślakṣṇam” means smooth; beautiful.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: ślakṣṇaṃ sundaram ||6||

entries.sanskrit: मार्गैः प्रकार-विशेषैः । तान् एवाह---स्वभाव-भूता ये गुणास् तेषां मार्गेण वृत्ति-भेदेन । भावोऽभिप्रायः । फल-सङ्कल्प-भेदाद् भक्ति-भेद इत्य् अर्थः ।
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: mārgaiḥ prakāra-viśeṣaiḥ | tān evāha---svabhāva-bhūtā ye guṇās teṣāṃ mārgeṇa vṛtti-bhedena | bhāvo’bhiprāyaḥ | phala-saṅkalpa-bhedād bhakti-bheda ity arthaḥ |
entries.literal_english: “Paths” means distinct modes. He specifies them: according to the path of the guṇas inherent in one’s nature, that is, according to differences of mental disposition. Bhāva means intention; differences in devotion arise from differences in the intended fruit.

entries.sanskrit: अभिसन्धाय सङ्कल्प्य । संरम्भी क्रोधी । भिन्न-दृक् भेद-दर्शी । यो भावं भक्तिं कुर्यात्, स त्रि-विधोऽपि तामसः ॥८॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: abhisandhāya saṅkalpya | saṃrambhī krodhī | bhinna-dṛk bheda-darśī | yo bhāvaṃ bhaktiṃ kuryāt, sa tri-vidho’pi tāmasaḥ ||8||
entries.literal_english: Abhisandhāya means having formed an intention; saṃrambhī means angry; bhinna-dṛk means one who sees difference. One who performs devotion with such an attitude is tāmasic in each of these three ways.

entries.sanskrit: पृथग्-भावो भेद-दर्शी ॥९॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: pṛthag-bhāvo bheda-darśī ||9||
entries.literal_english: Pṛthag-bhāva means one who sees separateness or difference.

entries.sanskrit: कर्म-निर्हारं पाप-क्षयम् । परस्मिन् परमेश्वरे । तद्-अर्पणं कर्मार्पणम्, भगवत्-प्रीतिम् उद्दिश्येत्य् अर्थः । यष्टव्यम् इति विधि-सिद्धिम् उद्दिश्येत्य् अर्थः । भेद-दर्शित्वम् अर्चादाव् अर्चनं च त्रिष्व् अपि समानम् । तद् एव तामसादि-भक्तिषु त्रयस् त्रयो भेदाः । तासु यथोत्तरं श्रैष्ठ्यम् । एवं च श्रवण-कीर्तनादयो नवापि प्रत्येकं नव-नव-भेदाः । तद् एव स-गुणा भक्तिर् एकाशीति भेदा भवति ॥१०॥
word_for_word: with the aim of pleasing Bhagavān
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: karma-nirhāraṃ pāpa-kṣayam | parasmin parameśvare | tad-arpaṇaṃ karmārpaṇam, bhagavat-prītim uddiśyety arthaḥ | yaṣṭavyam iti vidhi-siddhim uddiśyety arthaḥ | bheda-darśitvam arcādāv arcanaṃ ca triṣv api samānam | tad eva tāmasādi-bhaktiṣu trayas trayo bhedāḥ | tāsu yathottaraṃ śraiṣṭhyam | evaṃ ca śravaṇa-kīrtanādayo navāpi pratyekaṃ nava-nava-bhedāḥ | tad eva sa-guṇā bhaktir ekāśīti bhedā bhavati ||10||
entries.literal_english: Karma-nirhāra means removal of sin. “To the Supreme” means to the Supreme Lord. Offering to Him means offering one’s acts with the intention of pleasing Bhagavān; acting because “it ought to be worshipped” means aiming at fulfillment of an injunction. Seeing difference and worship of the image occur in all three guṇa-based forms. Thus tāmasic and the other forms each have three subdivisions; each succeeding one is superior. Likewise each of the nine practices beginning with hearing and chanting has nine subdivisions, so devotion conditioned by the guṇas has eighty-one varieties.

entries.sanskrit: निर्गुणा तु भक्तिर् एक-विधैव, ताम् आह---मद्-गुण-श्रुति-मात्रेणेति द्वाभ्याम् । मद्-गुण-श्रुति-मात्रेण मयि पुरुषोत्तमे मनो-गतिर् इति या भक्तिः सा निर्गुणस्य भक्ति-योगस्य लक्षणम् इत्य् अन्वयः । अविच्छिन्ना सन्तता । लक्षणं स्वरूपम् । अहैतुकी फलानुसन्धान-शून्या । अव्यवहिता भेद-दर्शन-रहिता च ॥११-१२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nirguṇā tu bhaktir eka-vidhaiva, tām āha---mad-guṇa-śruti-mātreṇeti dvābhyām | mad-guṇa-śruti-mātreṇa mayi puruṣottame mano-gatir iti yā bhaktiḥ sā nirguṇasya bhakti-yogasya lakṣaṇam ity anvayaḥ | avicchinnā santatā | lakṣaṇaṃ svarūpam | ahaitukī phalānusandhāna-śūnyā | avyavahitā bheda-darśana-rahitā ca ||11-12||
entries.literal_english: Guṇa-transcending devotion is only one kind. In the two verses beginning “merely by hearing My qualities,” the construction is: the movement of the mind toward Me, the Supreme Person, arising merely from hearing My qualities, is the defining nature of nirguṇa bhakti-yoga. It is uninterrupted and continuous, causeless in the sense of seeking no fruit, and unobstructed in the sense of being free from perception of difference.

entries.sanskrit: भक्तानां निष्कामतां कैमुत्य-न्यायेनाह---सालोक्यं मया सहैकस्मिन् लोके वासम्, सार्ष्टिं समानैश्वर्यम्, सामीप्यं निकट-वर्तित्वम्, सारूप्यं समान-रूपताम्, एकत्वं सायुज्यम् । उत अपि दीयमानम् अपि न गृह्णन्ति, कुतस् तत् कामनेत्य् अर्थः ।।१३॥
word_for_word: even when offered they do not accept
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: bhaktānāṃ niṣkāmatāṃ kaimutya-nyāyenāha---sālokyaṃ mayā sahaikasmin loke vāsam, sārṣṭiṃ samānaiśvaryam, sāmīpyaṃ nikaṭa-vartitvam, sārūpyaṃ samāna-rūpatām, ekatvaṃ sāyujyam | uta api dīyamānam api na gṛhṇanti, kutas tat kāmanety arthaḥ ||13||
entries.literal_english: By an argument from the greater to the lesser he shows the devotees’ freedom from desire. Sālokya is residence in one world with the Lord; sārṣṭi is equal sovereignty; sāmīpya is nearness; sārūpya is sameness of form; ekatva is sāyujya. Even when these are offered, devotees do not accept them—how much less would they desire them.

entries.sanskrit: किम् इति तर्हि भजन्ते भक्तेर् एव परम-फलत्वाद् इत्य् आह---स एवेति । ननु त्रै-गुण्यं हित्वा ब्रह्म-प्राप्तिः परम-फलं प्रसिद्धम् । सत्यम् । तत् तु भक्ताव् आनुषङ्गिकम् इत्य् आह---येन भक्ति-योगेन । मद्-भावाय ब्रह्मत्वाय ॥१४॥
word_for_word: because devotion itself is the supreme fruit
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kim iti tarhi bhajante bhakter eva parama-phalatvād ity āha---sa eveti | nanu trai-guṇyaṃ hitvā brahma-prāptiḥ parama-phalaṃ prasiddham | satyam | tat tu bhaktāv ānuṣaṅgikam ity āha---yena bhakti-yogena | mad-bhāvāya brahmatvāya ||14||
entries.literal_english: Why then do they worship? Because devotion itself is the supreme fruit. It is well known that transcending the three guṇas and attaining Brahman is the highest fruit; true, but in devotion that comes incidentally. Through this bhakti-yoga one attains mad-bhāva, the state of Brahman.

entries.sanskrit: एवं भूताया भक्तेः साधनान्य् आह पञ्चभिः । निषेवितेन सम्यग् अनुष्ठितेन। अनिमित्तेन स्व-धर्मेण नित्य-नैमित्तिकेन । महीयसा श्रद्धादि-युक्तेन । क्रिया-योगेन पञ्चरात्राद्य्-उक्त-पूजा-प्रकारेण । शस्तेन निष्कामेन ॥१५॥
word_for_word: by one’s own dharma without motive
endowed with faith and the like
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: evaṃ bhūtāyā bhakteḥ sādhanāny āha pañcabhiḥ | niṣevitena samyag anuṣṭhitena| animittena sva-dharmeṇa nitya-naimittikena | mahīyasā śraddhādi-yuktena | kriyā-yogena pañcarātrādy-ukta-pūjā-prakāreṇa | śastena niṣkāmena ||15||
entries.literal_english: In five verses he gives the disciplines for such devotion: one’s own dharma, properly performed without motive through obligatory and occasional duties; performed with greatness, meaning endowed with faith and the like; ritual worship according to the methods taught in the Pañcarātra and related texts; and conduct that is commendable because desireless.

entries.sanskrit: मद्-धिष्ण्यं मत्-प्रतिमादि तस्य दर्शनादिभिः । सत्त्वेन धैर्येण । असङ्गमेन वैराग्येण ॥१६॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: mad-dhiṣṇyaṃ mat-pratimādi tasya darśanādibhiḥ | sattvena dhairyeṇa | asaṅgamena vairāgyeṇa ||16||
entries.literal_english: Mad-dhiṣṇya means My image and other sacred abodes; one should engage in seeing and serving them. Sattva here means steadfastness, and asaṅgama means detachment.

entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara Svāmī explicitly gives no commentary here in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: आर्जवेन अकौटिल्येन ॥१८॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: ārjavena akauṭilyena ||18||
entries.literal_english: Ārjava means absence of crookedness, straightforwardness.

entries.sanskrit: मद्-धर्मणो भगवद्-धर्मानुष्ठातुः पुरुषस्याशयश् चित्तम् ॥१९॥
word_for_word: of one who performs the Lord’s dharma
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: mad-dharmaṇo bhagavad-dharmānuṣṭhātuḥ puruṣasyāśayaś cittam ||19||
entries.literal_english: For a person who performs the Lord’s dharma, āśaya means the mind or heart.

entries.sanskrit: प्रयत्नं विनैव प्राप्तौ दृष्टान्तः, वातो रथः प्रापको यस्य गन्धस्य । आशयात् स्थानात् । आवृङ्क्ते आत्म-सात्-करोति । अविकारि समं यच् चेतः ॥२०॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: prayatnaṃ vinaiva prāptau dṛṣṭāntaḥ, vāto rathaḥ prāpako yasya gandhasya | āśayāt sthānāt | āvṛṅkte ātma-sāt-karoti | avikāri samaṃ yac cetaḥ ||20||
entries.literal_english: An analogy shows attainment without effort: fragrance is carried from its place by the wind as its vehicle. Likewise the Lord appropriates a mind that is even and changeless.

entries.sanskrit: चित्त-शुद्धिश् च सर्व-भूतात्म-दृष्ट्यैव भवतीति वक्तुं केवल-प्रतिमादि-निष्ठां निन्दन्न् आह---अहम् इति सप्तभिः । अर्चा एव विडम्बनम् अनुकरणम् । अर्चायां पूजा-विडम्बनम् इति वा । अवज्ञोपेक्षा-द्वेष-निन्दाः क्रमेण चतुर्भिर् निषिध्यन्ते ॥२१॥
word_for_word: by seeing the Self in all beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: citta-śuddhiś ca sarva-bhūtātma-dṛṣṭyaiva bhavatīti vaktuṃ kevala-pratimādi-niṣṭhāṃ nindann āha---aham iti saptabhiḥ | arcā eva viḍambanam anukaraṇam | arcāyāṃ pūjā-viḍambanam iti vā | avajñopekṣā-dveṣa-nindāḥ krameṇa caturbhir niṣidhyante ||21||
entries.literal_english: To teach that purity of mind arises precisely from seeing the Self in all beings, he censures exclusive fixation on the image alone in seven verses beginning “I.” Arcā may mean merely an imitation, or the phrase may mean an imitation of worship in the image. Disrespect, neglect, hatred, and condemnation are prohibited successively in four verses.

entries.sanskrit: हित्वा उपेक्ष्य ॥२२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: hitvā upekṣya ||22||
entries.literal_english: Hitvā means having abandoned or neglected.

entries.sanskrit: द्रव्यैर् उत्पन्नया क्रियया । भूत-ग्रामावमानिनस् तन्-निन्दकस्य ॥२४॥
word_for_word: by ritual action produced through materials
of one who dishonors the aggregate of beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: dravyair utpannayā kriyayā | bhūta-grāmāvamāninas tan-nindakasya ||24||
entries.literal_english: “By substances” means by ritual action produced through material offerings. One who dishonors the aggregate of beings is one who condemns them.

entries.sanskrit: तर्हि किम् अर्चादाव् अर्चनम् अनर्थकम् एव ? नेत्य् आह---अर्चादाव् इति । सर्व-भूतेष्व् अवस्थितं मां स्व-हृदि यावन् न वेद । स्व-कर्म-कृत् कर्माविरोधेन यथावकाशम् । अनेन कर्म-निष्ठाया अपि स एवावधिर् इत्य् उक्तं भवति ॥२५॥
word_for_word: until one knows Me in one’s own heart
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tarhi kim arcādāv arcanam anarthakam eva ? nety āha---arcādāv iti | sarva-bhūteṣv avasthitaṃ māṃ sva-hṛdi yāvan na veda | sva-karma-kṛt karmāvirodhena yathāvakāśam | anena karma-niṣṭhāyā api sa evāvadhir ity uktaṃ bhavati ||25||
entries.literal_english: Is worship of the image then useless? No. One should worship until one knows Me, who dwell in all beings, within one’s own heart. “Doing one’s own work” means acting as opportunity permits without conflict with one’s prescribed duties. Thus even steadfastness in ritual action has this realization as its limit.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तरा अन्तरं भेदम् । उत् अपि । अरम् अल्पम् । अल्पम् अपि भेदं यः पश्यतीत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, अन्तरा मध्ये । उदरं शरीरम् । मृत्युर् अहं तस्य भयं विदधे कारोमि ॥२६॥
word_for_word: one who sees even slight difference
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: antarā antaraṃ bhedam | ut api | aram alpam | alpam api bhedaṃ yaḥ paśyatīty arthaḥ | yad vā, antarā madhye | udaraṃ śarīram | mṛtyur ahaṃ tasya bhayaṃ vidadhe kāromi ||26||
entries.literal_english: Antara means difference or interval. Aram means even a little: whoever sees even the slightest difference is subject to fear. Alternatively, antara means “within” and udara “body”; I, as Death, produce fear for him.

entries.sanskrit: अथ अतः सर्व-भूतेषु कृतालयं कृतावासम् । तत्र हेतुः---भूतानाम् आत्मानम् अन्तर्यामिणम् । अभिन्नेन चक्षुषा सम-दर्शनेन ॥२७॥
word_for_word: having made My dwelling in all beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: atha ataḥ sarva-bhūteṣu kṛtālayaṃ kṛtāvāsam | tatra hetuḥ---bhūtānām ātmānam antaryāmiṇam | abhinnena cakṣuṣā sama-darśanena ||27||
entries.literal_english: Therefore one should honor Me as having made My dwelling in all beings, because I am the inner controller and Self of beings, and one should see with an undivided eye—that is, with equal vision.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रापि यथोत्तरं मानाद्य्-अतिशयः कर्तव्य इति वक्तुं तारतम्यम् आह---जीवा इति सार्धैः षड्भिः । अजीवानाम् अचेतनेभ्यः । ततस् तेष्व् अपि प्राण-भृतः प्राण-वृत्तिम् अन्तः । स-चित्ता ज्ञान-वन्तः । इन्द्रियाणां वृत्तयो येषु । इन्द्रिय-वृत्तयो वृक्षाणाम् अपि सूक्ष्माः सन्त्य् एव । तथा हि महाभारते मोक्ष-धर्मेषु स्मर्यते, तस्मात् पश्यन्ति पादपास् तस्माज् जिघ्रन्ति पादपाः \[म।भा। १२.१७७.१४-१५\] इत्य्-आदि । प्रसिद्धा तु स्पर्शनेन्द्रिय-वृत्तिर् एव ॥२८॥
word_for_word: progressively greater honor in ascending order
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tatrāpi yathottaraṃ mānādy-atiśayaḥ kartavya iti vaktuṃ tāratamyam āha---jīvā iti sārdhaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ | ajīvānām acetanebhyaḥ | tatas teṣv api prāṇa-bhṛtaḥ prāṇa-vṛttim antaḥ | sa-cittā jñāna-vantaḥ | indriyāṇāṃ vṛttayo yeṣu | indriya-vṛttayo vṛkṣāṇām api sūkṣmāḥ santy eva | tathā hi mahābhārate mokṣa-dharmeṣu smaryate, tasmāt paśyanti pādapās tasmāj jighranti pādapāḥ \[ma|bhā| 12.177.14-15\] ity-ādi | prasiddhā tu sparśanendriya-vṛttir eva ||28||
entries.literal_english: To show that progressively greater honor is due in ascending order, he sets out a hierarchy in six and a half verses. Above nonliving things are those that sustain vital functions; above them are conscious beings possessing knowledge and functions of the senses. Even trees possess subtle sensory functions, as remembered in the Mokṣadharma; touch is simply the most evident among them.

entries.sanskrit: अतस् तेभ्यः स्पर्श-वेदिभ्यो रस-वेदिनो मत्स्यादयः श्रेष्ठाः । गन्ध-विदो भ्रम-रादयः । शब्द-विदः सर्पादयः ॥२९॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: atas tebhyaḥ sparśa-vedibhyo rasa-vedino matsyādayaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ | gandha-vido bhrama-rādayaḥ | śabda-vidaḥ sarpādayaḥ ||29||
entries.literal_english: Above beings that know touch are those such as fish that know taste; above them are those such as bees that know smell; and above them are beings such as snakes that know sound.

entries.sanskrit: रूप-भेद-विदः काकादयः । उभयतो दन्ताः येषाम् । अपादेभ्यो बहु-पादास् तेभ्यश् चतुष्-पादा इत्य् अर्थः । ततो द्विपान् मनुष्यः ॥३०॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: rūpa-bheda-vidaḥ kākādayaḥ | ubhayato dantāḥ yeṣām | apādebhyo bahu-pādās tebhyaś catuṣ-pādā ity arthaḥ | tato dvipān manuṣyaḥ ||30||
entries.literal_english: Those that distinguish forms, such as crows, are higher. “With teeth on both sides” describes another class. Above footless beings are many-footed beings, above them quadrupeds, and above them bipeds, namely human beings.

entries.sanskrit: ततस् तेषु वर्णाः ॥३१॥
entries.literal_english: “Then, among them, the varṇas [are four].” This continues the description of gradations among living beings.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: tatas teṣu varṇāḥ ||31||

entries.sanskrit: संशय-च्छेत्ता मीमांसकः । ततोऽपि केवलात् स्व-कर्म-कृत् । मुक्त-सङ्गस्य लक्षणम् आत्मनो धर्मम् अदोग्धा निष्काम इत्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: saṃśaya-cchettā mīmāṃsakaḥ | tato’pi kevalāt sva-karma-kṛt | mukta-saṅgasya lakṣaṇam ātmano dharmam adogdhā niṣkāma ity arthaḥ ||32||
entries.literal_english: The resolver of doubt is the Mīmāṃsaka. Higher even than the mere knower is one who performs his own prescribed action. One whose attachment is released does not milk his own dharma for personal gain; that is, he acts without desire.

entries.sanskrit: अर्पिता अशेषाः क्रिया अर्थास् तत्-फलान्य् आत्मा देहश् च येन, अत एव निरन्तरोऽव्यवहितः । अकर्तुः कर्तृत्वाभिमान-शुन्यात् ॥३३॥
word_for_word: free from the conceit of agency
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: arpitā aśeṣāḥ kriyā arthās tat-phalāny ātmā dehaś ca yena, ata eva nirantaro’vyavahitaḥ | akartuḥ kartṛtvābhimāna-śunyāt ||33||
entries.literal_english: For him all actions, their objects and fruits, and the body itself have been offered up; therefore he is nirantara, without separation. “Non-agent” means free from the conceit of being the doer.

entries.sanskrit: जीवानां कलया परिकलनेन अन्तर्यामितया प्रविष्ट इति दृष्ट्येत्य् अर्थः ॥३४॥
word_for_word: by His portions among living beings
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: jīvānāṃ kalayā parikalanena antaryāmitayā praviṣṭa iti dṛṣṭyety arthaḥ ||34||
entries.literal_english: The meaning is: one should see the Lord as having entered living beings by His portions—that is, by His presence as their inner controller.

entries.sanskrit:
उक्तं भक्ति-योगं पूर्वोक्तेनाष्टाङ्ग-योगेन सहोपसंहरति, भक्ति-योगश् चेति । हे मानवि
! पुरुषं परमेश्वरम् ॥३५॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
uktaṃ bhakti-yogaṃ pūrvoktenāṣṭāṅga-yogena sahopasaṃharati, bhakti-yogaś ceti | he mānavi
! puruṣaṃ parameśvaram ||35||
entries.literal_english: He concludes the bhakti-yoga just described together with the previously taught eight-limbed yoga. “O daughter of Manu,” puruṣa here means the Supreme Lord.

entries.sanskrit:
यद् अन्यत् पृष्टं जीवस्य संसृतीः कालस्य स्वरूपं चाचक्ष्वेति, तद् आह---एतद् इति सार्धेन । एतत् सर्व-नियन्तृ यद् भगवतो रूपम् । कीदृशम् ? प्रधान-पुरुषात्मकं परं तद्-व्यतिरिक्तं च । एतद् एव दैवम् इत्य् अभिधीयते । कीदृशम् ? कर्मणो विचेष्टितं नाना-संसृति-लक्षणं यस्मात् तत् । दैव-प्रेरित-कर्म-कृताः संसृतयो विचित्रा इत्य् अर्थः ॥३६॥

एतद् एव भगवतो रूपं काल इति चाभिधीयते । कीदृशम् ? रूप-भेदस्य वस्तूनाम् अन्यथात्वस्यास्पदम् आश्रयः कारणम् । उक्तं हि---कालाद् गुण-व्यतिकरः इति । वक्ष्यते च गुण-व्यतिकरः कालः इति । दिव्यम् अद्भुत-प्रभावम् । तद् एवाह---भूतानाम् इति यावत् समाप्ति । महद्-आदीनां तत्-तद्-अभिमानिनां जीवानाम् ॥३७॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
yad anyat pṛṣṭaṃ jīvasya saṃsṛtīḥ kālasya svarūpaṃ cācakṣveti, tad āha---etad iti sārdhena | etat sarva-niyantṛ yad bhagavato rūpam | kīdṛśam ? pradhāna-puruṣātmakaṃ paraṃ tad-vyatiriktaṃ ca | etad eva daivam ity abhidhīyate | kīdṛśam ? karmaṇo viceṣṭitaṃ nānā-saṃsṛti-lakṣaṇaṃ yasmāt tat | daiva-prerita-karma-kṛtāḥ saṃsṛtayo vicitrā ity arthaḥ ||36||

etad eva bhagavato rūpaṃ kāla iti cābhidhīyate | kīdṛśam ? rūpa-bhedasya vastūnām anyathātvasyāspadam āśrayaḥ kāraṇam | uktaṃ hi---kālād guṇa-vyatikaraḥ iti | vakṣyate ca guṇa-vyatikaraḥ kālaḥ iti | divyam adbhuta-prabhāvam | tad evāha---bhūtānām iti yāvat samāpti | mahad-ādīnāṃ tat-tad-abhimānināṃ jīvānām ||37||
entries.literal_english: Devahūti had also asked for an explanation of the living being’s transmigrations and the nature of Time. He now answers. This form of Bhagavān governs all; it comprises Pradhāna and Puruṣa yet is also beyond them. This is called daiva, destiny. From it comes the activity of karma manifesting as diverse courses of transmigration; thus the transmigrations produced by acts impelled by destiny are various.

entries.sanskrit: भय-हेतुत्वम् आह---य इति । भूतैर् एव भूतान्य् अत्ति संहरति । अधियज्ञो यज्ञ-फल-दाता । कलयतां वशी-कुर्वताम् ॥३८॥
word_for_word: he explains the cause of fear, beginning with “he who”
he consumes and dissolves beings by means of the beings themselves
as the Lord presiding over sacrifice, he gives the fruits of sacrifice
of those who control; bring under control
entries.literal_english: He explains why the Lord is a cause of fear: he consumes and dissolves beings by means of the beings themselves. As the presiding Lord of sacrifice, he gives the fruits of sacrifice. “Of those who control” refers to those whom he brings under his control.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: bhaya-hetutvam āha---ya iti | bhūtair eva bhūtāny atti saṃharati | adhiyajño yajña-phala-dātā | kalayatāṃ vaśī-kurvatām ||38||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara Svāmī explicitly gives no commentary here in the pinned source.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.

entries.sanskrit: भीषास्माद् वातः पवते इत्य्-आदि-श्रुति-प्रसिद्धम् एतस्य भीषणत्वम् अपि काल-रूपेणैवेत्य् आह---यद् इति षट्केन । यद्-भयात् यस्य प्रेरणात् वाति स्वल्पत्वेन बहुत्वेन दिग्-भेदेन च चलति तपति कुत्रचित् कदाचित् तापत-पूर्वकं प्रकाशयति उदयास्तमयत्वात् एवं भाति च ॥४०॥
word_for_word: the Śruti statement “from fear of him the wind blows” and the like is well known
even this fearful force is Time itself
thus he says, in the six verses beginning “from whose”
वाति स्वल्पत्वेन बहुत्वेन दिग्-भेदेन च चलति
the wind blows, moving gently or forcefully and in different directions
at some places and times it shines after heating
because of their rising and setting
thus the heavenly bodies also shine
entries.literal_english: The Śruti statement “From fear of him the wind blows” and the like is well known. The text says in the six verses beginning “from whose fear” that even this fearful force is Time itself. “From whose fear” means by whose prompting: the wind blows, moving sometimes gently and sometimes forcefully and in different directions; the sun burns and shines at different places and times; and, because they rise and set, the heavenly bodies likewise shine.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: bhīṣāsmād vātaḥ pavate ity-ādi-śruti-prasiddham etasya bhīṣaṇatvam api kāla-rūpeṇaivety āha---yad iti ṣaṭkena | yad-bhayāt yasya preraṇāt vāti svalpatvena bahutvena dig-bhedena ca calati tapati kutracit kadācit tāpata-pūrvakaṃ prakāśayati udayāstamayatvāt evaṃ bhāti ca ||40||

entries.sanskrit: यत् यस्माद् भीताः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: because they are afraid of him
entries.literal_english: “Because they are afraid of him.”
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: yat yasmād bhītāḥ ||41||

entries.sanskrit: यतो भीताः सरितः स्रवन्ति । इन्धे दीप्यते सह-गिरिभिर् भूः ॥४२॥
word_for_word: the earth together with its mountains
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: yato bhītāḥ saritaḥ sravanti | indhe dīpyate saha-giribhir bhūḥ ||42||
entries.literal_english: Out of fear of Time the rivers flow; the earth, together with its mountains, shines and remains active.

entries.sanskrit: अदो नभो यन्-नियमाद् यस्याज्ञया । महान् महत्-तत्त्वम् अङ्कुरात्मकं स्व-देहं लोकत्वेन तनुते विस्तारयति ॥४३॥
word_for_word: by whose rule, by whose command
expands into the form of the worlds
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: ado nabho yan-niyamād yasyājñayā | mahān mahat-tattvam aṅkurātmakaṃ sva-dehaṃ lokatvena tanute vistārayati ||43||
entries.literal_english: The sky acts by His command. Mahat-tattva, like a sprout, expands its own body into the form of the worlds.

entries.sanskrit: गुणाभिमानिनो गुण-नियन्तारो देवा ब्रह्मादयोऽस्य विश्वस्य सर्गादिषु प्रवर्तन्ते । अनु-युगं वारं वारम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४४॥
word_for_word: the gods who preside over and govern the qualities
engage in the creation and other operations of this universe
“anu-yugam” means again and again, in every age
entries.literal_english: The gods who preside over and govern the qualities, Brahmā and the others, engage in the creation and other operations of this universe. “Anu-yugam” means again and again, in every age.
entries.source_note: Exact Śrīdhara block restored from pinned source vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; phrase-level glosses follow the commentary.
transliteration: guṇābhimānino guṇa-niyantāro devā brahmādayo’sya viśvasya sargādiṣu pravartante | anu-yugaṃ vāraṃ vāram ity arthaḥ ||44||

entries.sanskrit: जनेन पित्रादिना जनं पुत्रादिं जनयन्न् आदिकृत् । मृत्युनान्तकम् अपि मारयन्न् अन्त-करः स्वयं त्व् अनादिर् अनन्तोऽव्ययश् च ॥४५॥
word_for_word: through a person such as a father
generating a person such as a son
through death, killing even the ender [Yama]
the one who brings everything to an end
entries.literal_english: Through a person such as a father, he generates a person such as a son, and is therefore the first creator. Through death he kills even the ender [Yama]; himself, however, he is beginningless, endless and imperishable.
